messages.content: Build a responsive personal portfolio website for freelance photographer Alex Rivera using vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Include a hero section with name and tagline, an About section, a gallery grid with 6 placeholder images, and a contact form (frontend only, no backend). Use a clean minimal design, mobile-responsive, and keep all code in separate index.html, style.css, script.js files. Return the complete runnable code.

Great. Now add two improvements to the same site: 1) A lightbox when clicking any gallery image — show large image with title and caption, with Next/Previous buttons and close on overlay click. 2) Category filtering with buttons All / Nature / Urban / Portrait and smooth filtering of the gallery. Keep the design consistent and update the existing files.

Perfect. One more realistic requirement for the same photographer site: Add client-side CSV backup/restore for the gallery metadata (fields: id, title, category, caption) plus drag-and-drop reordering. Specifically: An "Export CSV" button that downloads gallery.csv and an "Import CSV" file input that restores the gallery from a CSV. The CSV must correctly handle captions containing commas, double-quotes, and line breaks per RFC 4180 (quoted fields, doubled quotes), include a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it correctly, and be lossless on round-trip (Export -> Import should restore identical data). Also make the gallery cards draggable to reorder, and persist the order in localStorage so it survives page reload. Keep it vanilla JS with no external libraries.

**Designing a web layout**

I'm thinking about how to format this correctly with clear separators and code blocks for readability. Using simple headers like "index.html" followed by a code block sounds good. I'll craft minimal CSS with variables and a responsive design, maybe a hero section with a gradient background. A simple nav with anchor links could be beneficial, even if they didn't require it. For the gallery, I plan to use placeholder images and ensure good accessibility, including labels and validation for the contact form.**Planning a minimal design**

I’m considering a minimal design with a white background, black text, and subtle grey lines, using a simple brand accent color. I might stick with system fonts or refer to Google Fonts like "Poppins" or "Inter," but keeping it minimal means relying mostly on system stacks. For the hero section, I’ll include the name "Alex Rivera — Freelance Photographer" and a tagline such as "Capturing candid stories in natural light." Then, there will be call-to-action buttons linking to the gallery and contact sections. The code will be neatly organized into separate files to maintain clarity.**Implementing design details**

I'm planning to include color variables and implement a container width for the layout, focusing on the hero style, gallery grid, forms, and buttons. I’ll also establish responsive breakpoints at 768 and 1024 pixels, ensuring to add focus-visible outlines for accessibility.

In script.js, I want to implement smooth scrolling for internal links and maybe a gallery lightbox, even if they didn't explicitly ask. I'll handle contact form validation and use placeholder images with proper alt text. For gallery responsiveness, I’ll set the columns to adjust based on the device size. I aim to keep the code minimal!**Structuring the HTML layout**

I'm starting with the HTML structure, making sure to include essential elements like charset, viewport meta tags, and a title for "Alex Rivera | Photographer." I’m contemplating a favicon, but I might skip it for simplicity.

For the header, I plan to include the site logo and a navigation section. While they didn't specifically ask for a header nav, it's pretty standard. I’m thinking of keeping it simple with anchor links for mobile, avoiding complex JavaScript for navigation toggles. I'll go for minimalism in the design overall!**Creating the website structure**

I'm outlining sections for the website, starting with the hero section that introduces the freelance photographer, Alex Rivera, along with a tagline and action buttons. Next, there's an "About" section detailing services like portraits, events, and editorial work, followed by a gallery section for selected work.

The contact section includes a form for inquiries with required fields for name, email, and message, plus some basic validation. Additionally, I need to finalize the footer with textual social links and a copyright notice, ensuring accessibility and smooth scrolling functionality throughout the site.
